questions.stem: A 224×224×3 image enters a conv layer with 64 filters of size 7×7, stride 2, padding 3. What is the output shape?
questions.explanation: Spatial size is floor((H + 2p − k)/s) + 1 = floor((224 + 6 − 7)/2) + 1 = 112. Output depth is set by the filter count.
questions.source: Goodfellow, Bengio & Courville, Deep Learning — Ch. 9

questions.stem: Two stacked 3×3 convolutions cover the same receptive field as one 5×5. With C channels in and out, how do their parameter counts compare?
options: 18C² against 25C², so the stack is cheaper
25C² against 18C², so the stack is costlier
The stack uses 9C², a fourfold saving
questions.explanation: Two 3×3 layers need 2·9C² = 18C² weights against 25C² for a single 5×5, and the stack inserts an extra nonlinearity.
questions.source: Simonyan & Zisserman, Very Deep Convolutional Networks — §2.3
